running_pairs.rule: per-service running table from the signed action log, walked NEWEST entry first: (1) an entry that names services decides those services (compose_up -> attributed to that entry's (commit, file); compose_down -> gone) unless a newer entry already decided them; (2) an entry WITHOUT a services list is a whole-file compose up/down of that file: compose-manager runs `up -d --remove-orphans` under a per-model compose project, so every container of that file not in the new revision is removed and every service in it is re-created from it -- therefore once a whole-file entry for file F is seen, every OLDER entry for F is dead (ignored). A whole-file entry's service list is the service names of the file fetched at that commit. Report every distinct (commit, file) still attributed to a service, ordered by latest attributing compose_up desc; fetch raw.githubusercontent.com/nearai/cvm-compose-files/<commit>/<file>, require SHA256(body) == file_sha256; walk the WHOLE log (only whole-file entries need a fetch, for their service names; the walk is never cut short, and a whole-file entry whose file cannot be fetched still supersedes older entries of its file and is reported with services unknown); then hash-check up to 10 reported pairs, newest first (rows past the cap read "not fetched"); cache by (commit, file) with no expiry. Rule 3 (2026-11-06): EVERY compose_up runs with --remove-orphans whether or not it names services, so any up of file F at revision R removes F's containers whose service name is absent from R; walking newest-first, the INTERSECTION of the service sets of every newer up revision of F bounds what any older entry of F can still own (a middle revision that dropped S removed S's containers then, even if a later revision re-adds the name without naming or re-creating it); a name filtered out by that bound counts as DECIDED (retired) so that no older entry, of this or another file, can attribute it. This needs the service set of every up revision of F (fetched at its commit, cached). Cross-file eviction (two files sharing one project) is not derivable from the log and is NOT modelled.
running_pairs.why_changed: 2026-11-06: the previous rule attributed containers whose service names a later whole-file up of the SAME file no longer contained (renamed services), e.g. gpu02's DeepSeek DEP4x2 r1/r2 ranks after the 2026-10-31T00:17Z whole-file re-up that renamed them dp0..7 -- sixteen ranks on eight GPUs. compose-manager main.rs @c7fbaaf5 :1888-1899 and :1938-1949 document `--remove-orphans` under the per-model project. 2026-11-06 later: the first corrected derivation counted every fetch against the cap and stopped the walk, which dropped the still-running rotate-token (3c2f033b); ios found it. The cap applies to REPORTED pairs only. 2026-11-06 rule 3: on gpu13 the 2026-11-04 proxy-scoped up of small-models (320afade) removed the GLM-5.3 engine pair of the 10-27 revision (service names no longer in the file); GPU capacity confirms; no compose_down was logged. The fixture's four pairs are unchanged by rule 3. 2026-11-06 (ios): the bound is the intersection of all newer up revisions, and a filtered name is retired, not freed — otherwise mutation 9's r4 was re-attributed to an older TP2x4 entry.
running_pairs.liveness_rule: LEFTOVER / liveness undecidable, PER SERVICE (rule revised 2026-11-06, superseding the whole-file-only bound): the container of file F's service S, created by the entry that decided S at time t_S, is under the default-project reading removed as an orphan by the FIRST LATER compose_up of a DIFFERENT file G (scoped or whole-file: every up runs --remove-orphans) whose revision does not define the name S; under the per-model-project reading it persists. The log records no project, so S is undecidable; a name G's revision also defines is not an orphan and stays running; an up whose revision cannot be fetched counts as evicting (fail closed). A pair is LEFTOVER when every service attributed to it is undecidable; a pair with both keeps its running services and reports the others. Whole-file DOWNs of other files never count. LIVE REFUTATION: the proxy that answered THIS attestation report is alive now — the service(s) whose block sets MODEL_NAME=<report model_name> in the newest attributed revision. If a later up of another file G whose revision lacks that proxy's name exists, G demonstrably did not evict the proxy's file F: (F, G) is a refuted eviction and no up of G counts against any service of F (gpu13, 2026-11-04: prod/sage-pull.yaml was upped whole at 15:30:08Z after the 03:03:35Z small-models proxies, which answered on 11-06; without the refutation the whole serving stack reads undecidable). Downs carry no file_sha256: a whole-file down's service list is read from the file at its commit unhashed (commit-addressed over TLS); where an up in the same log pins the same (commit, file), hash-check against that up's file_sha256; a down can only retire services, never attribute one.

chat_path.rule: Per CVM and per connection HOST (never per model id: on gpu04 proxy-glm53 and proxy-glm53-long both declare MODEL_NAME=z-ai/glm-5.3-flash). (1) INGRESS: among the running revisions on the CVM (per-service running table from the signed log, running_pairs.rule), the service with published ports: whose nginx config has a server block whose server_name matches HOST (exact name or its ~^ regex forms); that block's `location /` proxy_pass target, or the `set $var http://<service>:<port>` it references in the same location, names the PROXY service. (2) the proxy's VLLM_BACKEND_URLS (comma-separated http://<service>:<port>), else VLLM_BASE_URL, names the ENGINE services; the literal default of ${VAR:-default} counts, an override is unrecorded. (3) PATH = {ingress, proxy, engines}; each path service maps to the (file, sha256) that created it (running table) and to the image it runs (a build: service -> its FROM digest). (4) a LEAKS page counts for this chat iff it is a recipe page whose exposure.services intersects PATH, or an image page (scope_kind image) whose digest a path service runs. The rollup is computed from on-path pages only; off-path LEAKS pages are 'not LEAKS for this chat'. (5) AMBIGUOUS (count every LEAKS page on the CVM): no server_name match for HOST, an unresolvable proxy_pass, a non-literal backend list, a path service with no attributed revision.

sheet_rows.rule: DISPLAY-ONLY filter over the per-service running table (running_pairs.rule, liveness_rule unchanged; the newest-first hash checks of all attributed pairs, cap 10, unchanged). The sheet lists ACTIVE INFRASTRUCTURE = (a) every service the log vouches for (attributed and not liveness-undecidable) UNION (b) every service on the chat PATH (chat_path.rule steps 1-3: ingress by server_name -> proxy_pass -> proxy -> VLLM_BACKEND_URLS / VLLM_BASE_URL -> engines), whether or not the log can vouch for it. Conditions on (b): (i) each path service is attributed by ITS OWN newest entry in the running table, and its row (file hash, image digest, audit page) is that revision's, never the proxy's revision; (ii) an upstream name counts only if the proxy's revision defines it as a service or the table has an attributing up for it, otherwise AMBIGUOUS; (iii) follow routers transitively (an upstream whose definition has its own VLLM_BACKEND_URLS / VLLM_BASE_URL, e.g. a vllm-proxy-rs image or a privacy filter) until an engine image, depth cap 4, beyond it AMBIGUOUS; (iv) the literal default of ${VAR:-default} counts and an env override is unrecorded (residual, unchanged). Everything else the log never closed (liveness undecidable, off path) is dropped from the sheet with no footnote. FALLBACK (chat_path.rule step 5, AMBIGUOUS): no server_name match for HOST, an unresolvable proxy_pass, a non-literal backend list, an upstream with neither definition nor attributing up, or depth exceeded -> show the FULL list (every attributed service, undecidable ones included) and count every LEAKS page on the CVM.
